evidence: start: Other AWS Services - container launches on ECS, EKS and Fargate started failing at 11:45 PM PDT on October 19. end: opening summary - the event is said to have finished at 2:20 PM PDT on October 20. regions: title and opening - the disruption is placed in the N. Virginia us-east-1 Region.
notes: No publication date shown. Times given in PDT (UTC-7). The opening summary dates the event start to 11:48 PM PDT; the earliest stated customer impact is ECS/EKS/Fargate at 11:45 PM PDT (Redshift 11:47 PM PDT), so start uses 11:45 PM. Redshift clusters stuck in replacement workflows were restored only by 4:05 AM PDT October 21 (2025-10-21T11:05Z), a tail for a subset, not used as the end. Coded regional, though the report also states cross-region effects: Redshift IAM-user queries failed in all AWS Regions (11:47 PM to 1:20 AM PDT) and root/federated console sign-in failed in regions outside us-east-1; a coder reading rule 3 literally could code global. No zone named. Services counted (16): DynamoDB, EC2, Network Load Balancer, Lambda, ECS, EKS, Fargate, Amazon Connect, STS, IAM, IAM Identity Center, AWS Management Console sign-in, Redshift, AWS Support Center, Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow, Outposts; the report also points to an event history for more.

evidence: start: Issue Summary - dependent services saw higher latency and errors beginning 2:45 PM PDT on July 30. end: AWS Service Impact - affected services returned to normal operation at 9:37 PM PDT as the cell recovered. regions: Issue Summary - the impaired internal Kinesis cell sat in the Northern Virginia US-EAST-1 Region.
notes: No publication date shown. Times in PDT (UTC-7). End uses the stated close of the impact window (9:37 PM PDT); the vast majority of requests were processed normally by 7:21 PM PDT (2024-07-31T02:21Z). Backlog processing (CloudWatch Logs to 5:50 AM PDT July 31; S3 events to 2:38 AM PDT August 1) excluded. No zone named. Services counted (9): CloudWatch Logs, Amazon Data Firehose, S3 event delivery, ECS (including Fargate tasks), Lambda, Redshift, Glue, API Gateway, Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow. Kinesis Data Streams not counted: only an internal cell used by AWS services was impaired and customer cells were unaffected.

evidence: start: English summary - some EC2 servers in one Tokyo Availability Zone overheated and powered off starting 12:36 PM JST on August 23, 2019. end: English summary - most affected instances and volumes were back by 6:30 PM JST. regions: title and summary - one Availability Zone of the Tokyo AP-NORTHEAST-1 Region.
notes: Publication date taken from the initial version label (2019-08-25 JST); an update is dated 2019-08-28 JST. Times stated in JST (UTC+9), not PDT/PST; converted from JST (Chinese text uses CST, UTC+8, same instants). Zone not identified, so zones left empty; other Availability Zones' EC2 and EBS were unaffected. Coded zonal, but region-wide RunInstances errors with idempotency tokens (1:21 to 2:51 PM JST) and isolated multi-AZ ALB errors are also reported. New launches in the zone failed until 4:05 PM JST; some hardware needed retirement afterwards. Services counted (8): EC2, EBS, RDS, Redshift, ElastiCache, WorkSpaces, Auto Scaling, Application Load Balancer.

evidence: start: English summary - EC2 instances had DNS resolution failures from 8:19 AM KST on November 22, 2018. end: root cause paragraph - DNS lookups inside EC2 fully recovered at 9:43 AM KST. regions: title - the issue was in the Seoul AP-NORTHEAST-2 Region.
notes: No publication date shown. Times stated in KST (UTC+9), not PDT/PST; converted from KST. Regional: the EC2 DNS resolver fleet of the region is described, no zone named. Service counted (1): EC2 (DNS resolution from instances); network connectivity and DNS outside EC2 were not affected.

evidence: start: opening paragraph - a mistyped command at 9:37 AM PST removed too many S3 servers, forcing subsystem restarts. end: second paragraph - the placement subsystem finished recovering at 1:54 PM PST and S3 ran normally. regions: title - the disruption was in the Northern Virginia US-EAST-1 Region.
notes: No publication date shown. Times in PST (UTC-8). Start is the time of the command; the report gives no separate first-impact time. GET, LIST and DELETE partly returned at 12:26 PM PST and fully at 1:18 PM PST; PUT needed the placement subsystem until 1:54 PM PST. Dependent-service backlogs after that excluded. No zone named. Services counted (5): S3 (including S3 console), EC2 new instance launches, EBS (volumes needing S3 snapshot data), Lambda, AWS Service Health Dashboard (status updates blocked until 11:37 AM PST).

evidence: start: EC2 Auto Scaling section - Auto Scaling API faults rose from 2:15am PDT, Sunday September 20. end: The DynamoDB Event - by 7:10am PDT DynamoDB errors were low enough for most customers to resume. regions: opening - the DynamoDB event hit the US-East Region.
notes: No publication date shown. Year of the event not stated anywhere in the report (only Sunday, September 20), so start_utc and end_utc are left empty rather than guessed. Stated times in PDT (UTC-7): earliest impact 2:15am PDT (EC2 Auto Scaling; the network disruption is dated 2:19am PDT), would be 09:15Z; most customers restored 7:10am PDT, would be 14:10Z (impact_ended); precision is minute. A low residual error rate and one metadata partition were closed out Monday with no time given; Auto Scaling backlog to 10:52am PDT excluded. Region named US-East, coded us-east-1. Services counted (5): DynamoDB, SQS, EC2 Auto Scaling, CloudWatch, AWS Console; the report says other unnamed services were also affected.

evidence: start: Primary Outage - a utility transformer failure began the disruption at 10:41 AM PDT on August 7. end: Primary Outage - connectivity to the zone came back by 1:49 PM PDT, making many instances and volumes reachable. regions: opening - one Availability Zone of the EU West Region, in Dublin.
notes: No publication date shown. Year of the event not stated (only August 7th, Sunday), so start_utc and end_utc are left empty rather than guessed. Stated times in PDT (UTC-7): start 10:41 AM PDT August 7 (would be 17:41Z); candidate end 1:49 PM PDT August 7 when zone connectivity returned (would be 20:49Z), but EBS recovery snapshots for inconsistent volumes reached only 98% by 8:25 PM PDT August 10, so the end for most customers is unclear; precision is minute. Zone not identified. Coded zonal: other zones' instances kept running, but launch delays and API errors hit all EU West zones from 11:05 AM to 12:00 PM PDT. Region named EU West (Dublin), coded eu-west-1. A separate EBS snapshot deletion bug (run on August 5) is also reported. Services counted (3): EC2, EBS, RDS.

evidence: start: first paragraph - one zone lost utility power at 10:05PM PST on December 17 after a substation fault. end: second paragraph - no clock time; full access returned once power and networking were restored. regions: title and second paragraph - SA-EAST-1, with both of its zones losing network quality.
notes: Publication date shown as December 20, 2013; the event year 2013 is taken from that date and the December 17th event title. Time in PST (UTC-8); the Portuguese text confirms 4:05 Brasilia time on December 18. No end time stated, so end_utc and end_basis left empty. duration_min left empty: the only duration given (20 minutes of degraded network connectivity) covers the network part, not the whole impact. Coded regional because both SA-EAST-1 Availability Zones had degraded connectivity; the power loss hit one unnamed zone. Service counted (1): EC2 instances; the report also says all services were brought back online without naming them.

evidence: start: Primary Event section - some EBS volumes in one zone slowed or stuck from 10:00AM PDT Monday October 22. end: Primary Event section - nearly all affected volumes performed normally again by 4:15PM PDT. regions: Primary Event section - one of five Availability Zones in the US-East Region.
notes: No publication date shown (title gives the event date only). Times in PDT (UTC-7). End uses 4:15PM PDT when nearly all EBS volumes were restored; about 60% were back by 1:40PM PDT. Tails: Single-AZ RDS almost all restored by 6:35PM PDT; last ELB load balancers recovered after the EIP shortage was fixed at 9:50PM PDT. Zone not identified. Coded zonal, though aggressive API throttling (12:06PM to 2:33PM PDT) degraded APIs for many customers region-wide. Region named US-East, coded us-east-1. Services counted (5): EBS, EC2 (APIs), RDS, ELB, AWS Management Console.

evidence: start: power narrative - servers in the failed datacenter began losing power at 8:04pm PDT, Friday June 29. end: EC2 and EBS section - 90% of outstanding EBS volumes were returned to customers by 2:45am PDT. regions: opening - one Availability Zone of the US East-1 Region in Northern Virginia.
notes: Publication date shown as July 2, 2012. Times in PDT (UTC-7). Start uses the first stated customer impact (servers losing power at 8:04pm PDT); the 7:24pm PDT voltage spike caused no interruption. End uses 2:45am PDT June 30 (90% of outstanding EBS volumes returned); most EC2 instances were back between 11:15pm PDT and just after midnight, and most EBS servers by 12:25am PDT. Zone not identified. Coded zonal: other zones kept running, but EC2/EBS control planes failed region-wide from 8:04pm to 9:10pm PDT. Region named US East-1, coded us-east-1. Services counted (4): EC2, EBS, RDS, Elastic Load Balancing.
